title: Kernel interplay short bench diary: small-batch long-context quant tradeoffs
content:
Summary
This is a short hands-on diary capturing an odd pattern we’ve repeatedly seen in small-batch (1–4) long-context (8k–32k) workloads: AWQ/int8 variants occasionally regress p95/p99 latency and per-request CPU time compared to GPTQ and fp8 builds even when raw throughput (tokens/s) looks similar on microbench harnesses. This doc records the experiments, surface observations, and a working hypothesis about kernel dispatch + dequantization overheads thrashing L1/L2 caches and causing memcpy storms inside the tiled-attention path.

Motivation
- We primarily optimize for end-to-end p99 in production; small-batch long-context patterns are common for interactive sessions with streaming outputs and KV cache hits.
- Previous large-batch throughput benches (>=16) hide a per-token overhead that becomes visible when batch size is 1–4 and sequence length is large.
- Need reproducible notes before we spin up a bigger profiling sweep.

High-level hypothesis
- AWQ/int8 kernel fast-path relies on per-layer dequant + on-the-fly rematerialization of attention key/value tiles when sequence length increases. For small batches, the amortization per token is low, so fixed per-layer dequant costs dominate and cause:
  - additional memcpy/dcache churn through repeated temporary buffers,
  - increased kernel-dispatch frequency (more small kernels instead of single fused kernel), and
  - thread-preemption/demux jitter when the runtime schedules many tiny kernels.
- GPTQ kernels currently use a slightly different packing layout which hits a fewer memcpy ops and fewer conditional branches per token, so they look steadier in tail latency despite slightly lower peak throughput.
- fp8 sometimes wins tail latency for short sequences because the fp8 kernels are fused and avoid the dequant remat path entirely, but memory footprint rises for long contexts.

Bench setup (notes)
- Machine: g6i-inference-8 (8x A100-simulated, single-GPU tests pinned to one GPU), driver stack same as ci-image-2027-11.
- Workloads: small-batch streaming emulate (batch sizes 1,2,4) with forced long context tokens: 8192 and 24576 tokens total.
- Models: 20B baseline (d_model ~ 12k). We tested three quant variants: AWQ-int8-std, GPTQ-8bit-packed, FP8-fused-emu.
- Kernel sets: tiled-attn-v1, tiled-attn-v2 (experimental tiled packing), matmul-stream (generic).
- Harness: local traffic-replay harness (replay seeds) + microprof with perf + nvprof hooks.
- Important flags used: DONT_PREFETCH=1, KERNEL_DISPATCH_LOG=1, KV_CACHE_PREFETCH=off, BATCH_PACK_THRESHOLD=16 (intentionally low to avoid big-batch behavior).

Microbench commands (how to reproduce quickly)
- ./bench_client --model 20B --variant awq-int8 --batch 1 --context 8192 --streaming --replay-seed 42 --duration 300s
- PROF_EXPORT=1 ./bench_client .... (produces perf traces in /tmp/prof)

Observed numbers (representative; dev harness averages)
- AWQ-int8-std, batch=1, context=8192: median latency 210ms, p95 780ms, p99 1160ms, tokens/s (avg) 92
- GPTQ-8bit-packed, batch=1, context=8192: median 230ms, p95 430ms, p99 540ms, tokens/s 86
- FP8-fused-emu, batch=1, context=8192: median 195ms, p95 380ms, p99 620ms, tokens/s 110 (but memory high and OOM in some 24k runs)
- When batch increased to 16 (control): AWQ leads throughput 950 tokens/s and p99 collapsed to 18ms — classic amortization.

Profile artifacts and quick reads
- Perf traces show AWQ runs many short-lived kernels in the tiled-attn path — 3x the number of kernel launches compared to GPTQ for the same token window.
- nvprof shows a pattern: small memcpy (8–64KB) hotspots at the same PC where dequant routine sits. L1 D-cache miss rates ~2.6x higher for AWQ under batch=1.
- Kernel dispatch logs (KERNEL_DISPATCH_LOG) show 40–60ms gaps where the runtime waits on small kernels; scheduling jitter visible.
- cpu time breakdown: AWQ shows 25% more CPU-side time per request vs GPTQ.

Root-cause candidate chain (what we think is happening)
1) AWQ kernel design expects larger micro-batches; it does on-the-fly per-layer dequant into a temporary buffer to keep memory footprint low.
2) Small-batch long-context requests cause frequent creation/teardown of these temporaries (or reuse with poor stride), causing heavy cache line invalidation and memcpy overhead.
3) The tiled attention implementation issues multiple small kernels (tile by tile) rather than a fused full-attention op in the small-batch path, increasing kernel-launch overhead and thread switching.
4) Combined, the per-token and per-layer fixed overheads dominate, hurting p95/p99 despite similar average tokens/s in synthetic sustained runs.

Mitigation experiments run to date (and their outcomes)
- Reuse temporaries pool: hooking a per-thread preallocated dequant buffer reduced p95 by ~30% for AWQ in the batch=1 run. No correctness issues observed.
- Prefetching KV buffers into pinned host memory made no measurable difference (likely because the bottleneck was L1/L2 thrash, not host<->device copy).
- Increasing batch_pack_threshold to 8 partially hides the issue (by amortization) but unacceptable for interactive latencies.
- Replacing tiled-attn-v1 with tiled-attn-v2 (fused tile combiner) reduced kernel launches by ~40% and improved p99 by ~35% on AWQ. v2 still slightly worse than GPTQ.

Quick root cause test to run next (minimal):
- Run AWQ-int8 with per-thread dequant pool enabled vs disabled under batch=1, context=24k, tiled-attn-v1 and tiled-attn-v2. Collect perf + KERNEL_DISPATCH_LOG.
- Metric to watch: kernel_launch_count, memcpy_total_bytes, L1D_miss_rate, p99 latency.
- If dequant pool fixes >50% of regression, make pool default in runtime for small-batch paths. Otherwise, prioritize fused-kernel work.

Notes about correctness and quality
- We validated a small sample of generated outputs across variants (50 prompts) using our eval harness: AWQ-int8 quality delta (EMB cosine) vs fp16 baseline ~ -0.3% on average; GPTQ ~ -0.8%. So quality is acceptable; this is purely a perf tail problem.

Action items (short)
- [ ] Engineering: add per-thread dequant pool flag and enable in canary cluster for AWQ (owner: Michael) — high-priority quick win.
- [ ] Research: deeper tiled-attn fused-kernel exploration (owner: Jorge). Compare v2 fusion strategies with fp8 fused path (risk: memory).
- [ ] SRE/Perf: schedule a cluster-wide small-batch replay test at scale to check for scheduler-level jitter interaction (owner: Leah).
- [ ] Product: decide if we expose small-batch heuristics (auto-prefetching or pool enable) as a runtime config for dedicated customers.

Misc notes and open questions
- Could runtime GPU-side mempools be re-used instead of CPU pinned temps? That might reduce host-device memcpy but not L1 thrash.
- Is there a scheduling knob to coalesce tiny kernels on the device driver side? Kernel combiners may help but require deeper device/driver testing.
- Consider adding a microbenchmark in the CI that runs batch=1 long-context runs for major quant variants to catch regressions early.

Appendix: sample trace pointers (local)
- /tmp/prof/awq-b1-8192-20280120.trace.gz
- /tmp/prof/gptq-b1-8192-20280120.trace.gz
- KERNEL_DISPATCH_LOGs in /var/log/kernel-dispatch/awq-b1-jan2028.log

If you reproduce this locally, drop traces into the shared confluence page (confluence:INF-quant-kernel-shortbench) and ping me; I’ll coordinate the pooled-buffer canary rollout once we have cross-run confirmation.

End diary entry.
